subject: Post-call: deployment fit & operational checklist (hosted / dedicated / private)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Turner <elise.turner@acmecorp.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks — quick recap and suggested next steps

Hi Elise / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the level-setting on Acme Commerce's production priorities. Below is a short recap and my proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Recap (from our conversation)
- Primary goal: add an LLM-powered product search assistant with sub-second interactive responses for 95% of queries and strong PII isolation for customer order data.
- Traffic profile: steady ~12k requests/day with 10–20% peak bursts during promotions; typical prompt lengths 40–120 tokens, embeddings for similarity at ~2k/day.
- Security & compliance: SOC2 evidence, KMS/TLS, VPC peering required for production.
- Concern flagged: "noisy neighbor" behavior on shared infrastructure — want guarantees around per-tenant SLOs and predictable tail latency.

Deployment options we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest to production, easy scaling, but multi-tenant runtime — mitigations include model-version pinning and per-tenant KV caching.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for Acme with predictable throughput and isolation at the allocation layer (recommended for predictable SLAs).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed control plane optional; best for strict regulatory or network-controlled workflows.

My proposals / requested next steps
1) Quick ops checklist workshop (45 min) — review p95/p99 latency targets, expected concurrency, and failure modes so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated sizing.
2) Technical deep-dive (joint with infra) — Sergio to run through resource isolation model and runtime-level QoS.
3) Security packet exchange — we will share SOC2 summary + suggested VPC architecture; please share any internal InfoSec checklist items.
4) Pricing ballpark for Dedicated reserve + pilot window (we'll provide a 30-day evaluation quote).

Attachments: redwood-deployment-comparisons.pdf (high-level tradeoffs), acme-map-of-requirements.xlsx (notes from call)

Can you confirm availability for the ops checklist this week (Thu/Fri) or Monday next week? We can slot Sergio and Monica from infra.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful. Quick replies inline: 

- Ops checklist: Thu (3/21) afternoon works for us, 2–3pm PT.
- Latency targets: our product PM wants p95 < 200ms and p99 < 500ms for the search assistant under typical load; during promotions we can tolerate p95 up to 300ms for a short window.
- Isolation: we need documented isolation boundaries (compute, KV cache, and model weights) and a clear escalation path if noisy neighbors cause SLO degradation. SOC2 and a KMS integration are must-haves.
- Pilot: we prefer a short Dedicated pilot to validate tail latency before committing to a longer reserved contract.

Attaching our internal ops checklist (see acme-map-of-requirements.xlsx).

Subject: Internal: Acme follow-up — workshop + mitigation options

Folks —

Following the call with Acme (see thread above). They want p95 < 200ms / p99 < 500ms with a preference for a short Dedicated pilot to validate tails before any reserved commitment. Key asks: documented isolation boundaries + clear escalation flow when noisy neighbor events occur.

Proposed internal agenda for Thu 3/21 2pm PT (ops checklist):
- Sergio: brief on runtime isolation primitives (dedicated pools, soft-tenancy, per-tenant cpu/gpu quotas, KV cache sharding).
- Monica: how we instrument scheduled perf tests and vendor-side tracing (token-level latency breakdown) so Acme can see p95/p99 in Console.
- Ben: pricing outline for a 30-day Dedicated pilot + criteria for success (SLOs, request volumes, rollback plan).

Risk/mitigation notes (draft to refine in meeting):
- Noisy neighbor risk: occurs when other tenants' concurrent batches inflate queue latency. Mitigations:
  * Dedicated pools (hard isolation) — preferred for strict SLOs.
  * Per-tenant reservation + admission control (soft isolation) — faster ramp to prod for lower commit.
  * Runtime admission QoS: priority queues, request preemption, and tail-aware batching.
  * Fallback routing to smaller/cheaper model variant when tail latency spikes to protect user experience.

Action: I'll confirm the meeting invite; Sergio / Monica / Ben please add one-slide notes on each mitigation and we will share with Acme during the workshop.

-Vanessa

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Elise Turner <elise.turner@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment fit & operational checklist (hosted / dedicated / private)

Thanks Vanessa. Quick technical clarifications for the meeting and to address "noisy neighbor" concerns up-front: 

1) Isolation primitives we will show:
- Dedicated capacity: physical GPU pool assignment + tenant-level network isolation. Guarantees: deterministic allocation of GPU memory and throughput; minimal cross-tenant interference.
- Soft-tenancy (hosted): per-tenant token budgeting, per-request queue timeouts, and a per-tenant KV shard to avoid cold-KV cross-talk.

2) Measurable SLOs / telemetry we can offer in pilot:
- p95/p99 token generation latency (per-route and per-tenant)
- Token-level time splits: model compute vs batch queue vs network vs kv-lookup
- Alerts + audit trail: tenant-scoped traces, request ids, and optional webhook to Acme's monitoring.

3) Pilot recommendation: 30-day Dedicated pool with a small reserve (1–2 GPUs equivalent) + synthetic traffic ramp to validate tails. Success criteria: sustained p95 < 200ms and p99 < 500ms at Acme's steady concurrency; ability to reproduce noisy neighbor injection test.

I'll prepare a 3-slide appendix: (a) isolation architecture diagram, (b) example Console telemetry screenshots, (c) suggested test plan (JIRA-INF-4821).

Elise — I've tentatively booked Thu 3/21 2pm PT (invitation should be in your calendar). If that slot doesn't work, we'll move to Mon.
